  "text": "Mara had left the book on the librarian’s desk. She was certain of it. Still, she searched her room, then the garden, where the stone sat among the beans like an ugly gray egg.

At dusk, brick walls rose on the empty lot again. The librarian stood behind his desk, holding out his hand.

“I don’t have it,” Mara said.

He looked past her, toward the river. “Then someone else does.”

Mara found her brother on the bank, reading a book with tomorrow’s date on its spine. He snapped it shut when he saw her.

“Where did you get that?”

“It was under the stone.” His face was pale. “It says the fence falls on you.”

Mara thought of the rotten post they had meant to replace. “Then we’ll stay away from it.”

“That’s what I said about the river.” He tucked the book under his arm. “But you came here anyway.”

Together they returned to the library. The clock above the desk showed one minute until closing. Mara’s brother set the book down, but the librarian did not reach for it.

“One of you may borrow it,” he said. “Or you may leave it here.”

Mara looked at her brother. He looked at the closed cover, then pushed it across the desk.

Outside, the library vanished behind them. They walked home by the long road, away from the river and the fence. In the morning, they would ask their neighbors to help replace the post. Tonight, neither of them wanted to know what tomorrow held."
